Build a 2D OpenFOAM case for the classic de Vahl Davis natural convection benchmark in a square cavity filled with air.
Use the solver buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam.
Define the geometry as a square cavity with side length L = 0.1 m in the x and y directions, with zero thickness in z (2D).
Apply the Boussinesq approximation for buoyancy with gravity vector g = (0, -9.81, 0).
Use standard air properties evaluated at the mean temperature of 295 K: density rho ≈ 1.225 kg/m³, thermal conductivity k ≈ 0.0262 W/m/K, dynamic viscosity mu ≈ 1.846e-5 Pa·s, specific heat Cp ≈ 1007 J/kg/K, Prandtl number Pr ≈ 0.71, thermal expansion coefficient beta ≈ 3.39e-3 1/K.
Set the left wall temperature to fixedValue 300 K.
Set the right wall temperature to fixedValue 290 K.
Set the top and bottom wall temperature to zeroGradient (adiabatic, no heat flux).
Set velocity boundary conditions to noSlip on all four walls.
Initialize the field with a uniform temperature of 295 K and zero velocity everywhere.
Generate a uniform 128×128×1 structured hexahedral mesh, ensuring at least 5 to 6 cells resolve the thermal boundary layer adjacent to the hot and cold vertical walls.
Run the simulation to steady state using PIMPLE time-stepping with sensible initial time step (e.g. 1e-4 s) and adaptive time stepping to accelerate convergence.
Monitor residuals and key quantities (centerline temperature profiles, center velocity) to confirm a steady convection cell has formed consistent with Ra ≈ 1.7e5.
